mcqs.learning_point: Compare data sets using standard deviation
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes how standard deviation is used to compare the spread of two data sets?

options.A: The data set with the larger mean always has the larger spread.
options.B: The data set with the larger standard deviation has the greater spread.
options.C: The data set with the smaller range has the larger spread.
options.D: Standard deviation cannot be used to compare spreads of data sets.

mcqs.answer: The data set with the larger standard deviation has the greater spread.
mcqs.explanation: Standard deviation measures the average distance of data points from the mean. A larger standard deviation indicates that the values are more widely dispersed, i.e., the data set has a greater spread. Hence option B is correct. Option A confuses mean with spread, option C misinterprets range, and option D is false because standard deviation is a standard measure of spread.

mcqs.question: If a set of lengths is recorded in centimeters, what will be the unit of its standard deviation?
mcqs.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance. Since variance has the square of the original unit (cm²), taking the square root returns the original unit, centimeters. Therefore the standard deviation is expressed in cm. Options A and C are units of area and volume, and D is incorrect because the measure retains the original unit.

mcqs.question: Data Set A: 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. Data Set B: 2, 8, 9, 10, 20. Which set shows greater consistency (i.e., less spread) based on standard deviation?

options.D: Consistency cannot be judged without the mean

mcqs.explanation: Data Set A values are evenly spaced around the mean (9) and have a relatively small standard deviation. Data Set B contains values far from the mean (2 and 20), giving it a larger standard deviation. Hence Data Set A is more consistent. Option B is opposite, C is false, and D is unnecessary because standard deviation already accounts for the mean.

mcqs.question: A teacher says, “Standard deviation is the positive square root of variance.” Which of the following best defines standard deviation?

options.A: The average of all data values
options.B: The square root of the sum of the squared data values
options.C: The positive square root of the variance of the data set
options.D: The difference between the maximum and minimum values

mcqs.answer: The positive square root of the variance of the data set
mcqs.explanation: By definition, variance is the average of the squared deviations from the mean. The standard deviation is the positive square root of this variance, giving a measure in the same unit as the original data. Options A, B, and D describe other concepts (mean, sum of squares, range).

mcqs.question: For a sample of 5 observations, a student computes the standard deviation by dividing the sum of squared deviations from the mean by 5 and then taking the square root. Is this procedure correct?

options.A: True, because the divisor is always the number of observations
options.B: False, because the sum of squared deviations should be divided by (n‑1) for a sample
options.C: False, because the square root must be taken before dividing
options.D: True, because variance uses n as the divisor

mcqs.answer: False, because the sum of squared deviations should be divided by (n‑1) for a sample
mcqs.explanation: When calculating the sample standard deviation, the unbiased estimator of variance uses n‑1 (degrees of freedom) as the divisor. Dividing by n gives the population variance, not the sample variance. Hence option B is correct. Options A and D ignore the n‑1 correction, and C reverses the order of operations.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare data sets using standard deviation
mcqs.question: Two data sets have the same mean, but Set X has a standard deviation of 4 and Set Y has a standard deviation of 1. Which statement is true?

options.A: Set X’s data points are more clustered around the mean than Set Y’s
options.B: Set Y’s data points are more dispersed than Set X’s
options.C: Set X exhibits greater variability than Set Y
options.D: Both sets have identical variability because their means are equal

mcqs.answer: Set X exhibits greater variability than Set Y
mcqs.explanation: A larger standard deviation indicates greater variability (more spread) around the mean. Therefore Set X, with SD = 4, is more variable than Set Y, with SD = 1. Options A and B invert the relationship, and D incorrectly assumes mean equality implies equal spread.

mcqs.question: Data set P is measured in kilograms and has a standard deviation of 2 kg. Data set Q is measured in grams and has a standard deviation of 1500 g. Which statement correctly compares their spreads?

options.A: Data set P has the larger spread because 2 kg (2000 g) > 1500 g
options.B: Data set Q has the larger spread because 1500 g > 2 kg
options.C: Both data sets have the same spread after unit conversion
options.D: The spreads cannot be compared because the units differ

mcqs.answer: Data set P has the larger spread because 2 kg (2000 g) > 1500 g
mcqs.explanation: To compare spreads, convert to the same unit. 2 kg equals 2000 g, which is greater than 1500 g, so Data set P is more spread out. Option B reverses the conversion, C is false, and D ignores the possibility of unit conversion.

mcqs.question: In a competitive exam, two groups of measurements are reported. Group A has a standard deviation of 1.2 cm, while Group B has a standard deviation of 3.5 cm. Which interpretation is correct?

options.A: Group A is more consistent (less spread) than Group B
options.B: Group B is more consistent (less spread) than Group A
options.C: Both groups are equally consistent because they measure the same quantity
options.D: Consistency cannot be inferred from standard deviation

mcqs.answer: Group A is more consistent (less spread) than Group B
mcqs.explanation: A smaller standard deviation indicates that the data points are closer to the mean, reflecting higher consistency. Hence Group A, with SD = 1.2 cm, is more consistent than Group B, which has SD = 3.5 cm. Options B, C, and D are incorrect for the reasons stated.
